skills.name: Investment transactions: contributed and subsidised assets, financial assets

note.text:
• Contribution of a fixed asset: the owner brings an asset (a car, a building) instead of money. It is recorded at its value: debit the asset account, credit 101 Capital.
• Fixed assets financed by a subsidy: the asset is recorded normally (debit class 2); the subsidy received is credited to account 14 Investment subsidies.
• Financial assets (account 27): shares bought in another company to keep for a long time, long-term loans given, deposits and guarantees paid (for example a rent deposit).
Example: the owner contributes a pick-up worth 4 000 000 FCFA: debit 245 Transport equipment 4 000 000; credit 101 Capital 4 000 000.

worked_example.problem: The owner contributes a pick-up worth {v} FCFA. Write the entry.
steps: The business receives a vehicle: debit {245} Transport equipment {v}.
It is the owner's contribution: credit {101} Capital {v}.

cards.idea: A contribution of an asset: debit the asset, credit {101} Capital.
A subsidy for an asset is credited to {14} Investment subsidies.
example: The asset is recorded in class {2}.

check.prompt: A business buys a machine for {p} FCFA and receives a State subsidy of {s} FCFA for it. How much does the business finance itself?

misconceptions.explain: The subsidy reduces what the business pays.

solution: The subsidy pays part of the cost.

cards.idea: Financial assets ({27}): long-term shares, loans given, deposits paid.

pick.r: shares bought in another company to keep long-term

pick.q: A business pays a rent deposit to its landlord. What is it?

right.text: A contributed asset is credited to capital.
Subsidies for assets go to account 14.
Shares kept long-term are financial assets.
A rent deposit is a financial asset.

wrong.text: A contributed car is credited to 701 Sales.
A subsidy must be recorded as a purchase of goods.
Financial assets are stocks of goods.
